title: Bug Catcher Checkpoint
intro: Catch errors before they crash your program, and pull in modules other people already wrote. Eleven rounds across both lessons. Get them right on the first try to earn ⭐⭐⭐!

rounds.prompt: Which pair safely handles code that might fail?
rounds.explain: try runs the risky code and except catches the error, so the program keeps going instead of stopping.
The division fails, so Python abandons the try block and runs the except block instead.
The try block gives up at the failing line. B is inside the block below it, so it never runs at all.

rounds.prompt: The try block works perfectly. What prints?
rounds.explain: With no error there is nothing to catch, so the except block is skipped. Dividing with / always gives a float, hence 5.0.
The value is the wrong sort of thing to turn into a number, so it is a ValueError. Naming it lets you give the user a useful message.

rounds.prompt: Why is  except ValueError:  usually better than a bare  except:  ?
options: It only catches that one problem, so other bugs are not hidden
It catches more kinds of error
rounds.explain: A bare except swallows everything, including mistakes you would rather find out about, and can only offer one vague message.
math.sqrt finds the square root and always hands back a float, so it prints 4.0 rather than 4.

rounds.prompt: This stops with a NameError. Pick the fix.
options: Add import random at the top
rounds.explain: Until the import line runs, the name random does not exist. Import lines belong at the very top of the file.

rounds.prompt: Which of these can random.randint(1, 6) never give you?
rounds.explain: randint includes both ends, so 1 and 6 are both possible. This is where it differs from range(1, 6), which stops at 5.

rounds.prompt: Match each piece to what it does.

pairs.right: Holds the code that might fail
Runs only when something went wrong

rounds.explain: The first four are the error-handling half of the module and the last two are the ready-made code half.

rounds.prompt: Build a try/except that warns when dividing by zero, and prints a message afterwards either way.
rounds.explain: The risky line goes under try, the rescue under except, and the final line sits outside both so it runs whatever happened.
